guard: a manager never ends its own process over its liveness lease: on unknown it keeps serving and retrying, on gone it re-acquires, on taken it warns and keeps serving, and the operator gets one line per state change while the ordinary shutdown path stays destructive
why: NO BUILD IN `command`, AND THAT IS A CLAIM THIS RUN CHECKS RATHER THAN ASSUMES. The suite
imports the subject RELATIVELY (`../src/manager.js`), so tsx loads `manager.ts` itself and a
mutation on it is live with no `dist` in the path. `@cotal-ai/core` is imported for TYPES only
and every plane the cells touch is stubbed, so no built artifact sits between the mutation and
the run. If that were wrong, mutation 1 would come back SURVIVED.
MUTATION 1 IS THE DEFECT IN ITS SHORTEST FORM: the process ends when the broker cannot be asked.
The shipped code waited one TTL first; the wait is not what the suite grades, the exit is.
MUTATION 2 DROPS THE RE-ACQUIRE. The process survives a gone key but never puts it back, so the
class scatter reads the instance as dead and a same-id restart is free to take the key while this
one is still serving. Every process-and-children cell stays green; only the re-acquire cell reddens.
MUTATION 3 REMOVES THE THROTTLE. Correct behaviour, and an outage of hours becomes fourteen
thousand identical lines in `manager.log`, which is how the motivating incident was read: by
searching a log for the one line that mattered.
MUTATION 4 IS THE CONTROL AND ALSO A REAL INVARIANT. It makes the EXPLICIT reap path leave
the children running. Every lease cell stays green and only the control cell reddens, which proves
the `stops` counter fires (so the zeros in the graded cells are earned) and that `cotal down
--with-agents` still reaps. Ordinary `stop()` leaving children is the #964 default, not a defect.

mutations.name: the defect restored: an unanswerable broker ends the process
mutations.expectRed: unknown: the process is not ended
mutations.cell: unknown: the process is not ended
mutations.note: The exit the shipped code reached one tick past the TTL, taken on the first tick instead. What the suite grades is that no tick may reach it.

mutations.name: a gone key is never put back
mutations.expectRed: gone: the key is put back (acquire called once) and the new revision is adopted
mutations.cell: gone: the key is put back (acquire called once) and the new revision is adopted
mutations.note: The half fix: survive the expiry, forget to re-register liveness. The revision is faked to the value the cell expects so that only the acquire count can catch it.

mutations.name: the state-change throttle is removed, so every tick prints
mutations.expectRed: unknown: repeated ticks in the same state print nothing more
mutations.cell: unknown: repeated ticks in the same state print nothing more
mutations.note: Correct decision, unreadable log. A careless edit rather than a malicious one.

mutations.name: CONTROL and invariant: the explicit reap path leaves every agent running
mutations.expectRed: CONTROL: the explicit reap path stops the child
mutations.cell: CONTROL: the explicit reap path stops the child (instrument fires)
mutations.note: Doubles as the positive control for the `stops` counter and as the guard on the opposite failure: an operator who asked for `--with-agents` must get a reap. Anchored on the withAgents true call, which is unique in the file.
